subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Oncologic emergencies: tumour lysis syndrome, hypercalcaemia, cord compression and vascular crises

steps.tx: **Tumour lysis syndrome** diagnostic criteria, established by the **Cairo-Bishop** laboratory classification, require two or more metabolic derangements within 3 to 7 days of starting therapy: hyperuricaemia, hyperkalaemia, hyperphosphataemia, and secondary hypocalcaemia. Massive intracellular lysis releases vast ionic contents into the bloodstream, overwhelming renal clearance and triggering life-threatening cardiac dysrhythmias and acute renal failure.

rows: Intrarenal tubular uric acid crystallization and acute obstruction
Peaked T waves, ventricular arrhythmias, sudden cardiac arrest
Calcium phosphate precipitation in microvasculature and nephrons

steps.tx: This figure groups five **oncological emergencies** with the first action for each. **Tumour lysis syndrome** shows the four electrolyte shifts with aggressive fluids as the backbone. Malignant hypercalcaemia pairs saline resuscitation with bone targeted therapy. Cord compression pairs immediate steroids with urgent whole spine imaging. Obstruction of the great vein and neutropenic fever complete the set with positioning and cultures before antibiotics.
steps.say: Take each panel in turn and state its emergency before looking at the action. For tumour lysis syndrome, list the four electrolyte shifts and explain why fluids lead. For hypercalcaemia, cord compression, great vein obstruction and neutropenic fever, give the single first step the figure shows. Finish by naming which panel needs steroids at once and which needs imaging within the day.

vis.alt: Five panels for tumour lysis syndrome, malignant hypercalcaemia, spinal cord compression, superior vena cava obstruction and febrile neutropenia with first actions.
vis.caption: Five oncological emergencies and their first actions.

steps.tx: **Rasburicase**, a recombinant **urate oxidase** enzyme, rapidly catalyses the enzymatic oxidation of poorly soluble uric acid into highly soluble allantoin, which is easily cleared by the kidneys. Unlike allopurinol, which only blocks further synthesis via xanthine oxidase, rasburicase directly dissolves pre-existing uric acid deposits, preventing acute obstructive uric acid nephropathy.
steps.say: Rasburicase, a recombinant urate oxidase enzyme, rapidly catalyses the enzymatic oxidation of poorly soluble uric acid into highly soluble allantoin, which is easily cleared by the kidneys. Unlike allopurinol, which only blocks further synthesis via xanthine oxidase, rasburicase directly dissolves pre-existing uric acid deposits, preventing acute obstructive uric acid nephropathy.

left.title: Allopurinol (Xanthine Oxidase Inhibitor)
points: Inhibits new synthesis of uric acid
Does not degrade existing circulating uric acid
Causes accumulation of insoluble xanthine and hypoxanthine
Takes 2 to 3 days to lower uric acid levels

right.title: Rasburicase (Recombinant Urate Oxidase)
points: Direct enzymatic catabolism into soluble allantoin
Rapidly lowers plasma uric acid within 4 hours
Single dose 0.15 to 0.20 mg/kg is highly effective
Contraindicated in G6PD deficiency due to methemoglobinemia

steps.tx: **Hypercalcaemia of malignancy** is driven primarily by tumour secretion of parathyroid hormone-related protein in over 80% of clinical cases, inducing osteoclast activation and renal calcium reabsorption. Emergent treatment requires vigorous volume expansion with isotonic saline to restore glomerular filtration, accompanied by intravenous **zoledronic acid** 4 mg or subcutaneous denosumab 120 mg to arrest osteolysis.

nodes.label: Zoledronic Acid 4 mg IV or Denosumab

steps.tx: **Malignant spinal cord compression** classically presents with progressive, localized nocturnal back pain that heralds motor weakness, sensory levels, and sphincter incontinence. Administering high-dose intravenous **dexamethasone** at 10 to 16 mg immediately reduces vasogenic edema and preserves neuronal viability, pending emergent spinal magnetic resonance imaging and urgent neurosurgical decompression or stereotactic radiotherapy.

steps.tx: **Superior vena cava** syndrome arises from mediastinal malignancy compressing the thin-walled thoracic vena cava, producing facial edema, dilated chest wall collateral veins, and respiratory compromise. In symptomatic obstruction from non-small cell lung cancer or refractory tumours, emergency percutaneous **endovascular stenting** provides instantaneous, durable hemodynamic and symptomatic relief superior to delayed radiation alone.

rows: Rapid restoration of venous return; first-line for severe airway or cerebral edema
Chemosensitive tumours (small cell lung cancer, high-grade lymphoma, germ cell)
Radioresponsive solid tumours without prior stenting or histological tissue diagnosis

steps.tx: **Hyperviscosity syndrome** in Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia or multiple myeloma results from extreme circulating paraproteins that elevate serum viscosity, causing headache, retinal hemorrhages with dilated sausage-link veins, and stupor. Emergency **plasma exchange** swiftly clears intravascular immunoglobulin pentamers, reducing whole-blood viscosity and reversing impending cerebrovascular infarction.

right.title: Emergency Management
points: 1 to 1.5 plasma volume exchange per procedure
Immediate reduction in serum IgM levels
Avoid red cell transfusions before pheresis

steps.tx: **Leukostasis syndrome** develops in acute myeloid leukaemia when circulating blast counts surge above 100 x 10^9/L, generating intravascular microvascular plugging and tissue hypoxia in pulmonary and cerebral microvascular beds. Urgent reduction of circulating blasts using high-dose oral **hydroxyurea** or intravenous cytarabine, accompanied by aggressive hydration, halts microvascular occlusion and fatal intracranial hemorrhage.

steps.tx: Malignant **pericardial tamponade** manifests through the classic **Beck triad** of profound arterial hypotension, elevated jugular venous distension, and muffled cardiac heart sounds, exacerbated by prominent pulsus paradoxus. Large malignant pericardial effusions compromise diastolic ventricular filling, demanding emergent echo-guided subxiphoid pericardiocentesis with prolonged catheter drainage to avert cardiovascular collapse.

rows: Direct reflection of intrapericardial pressure exceeding ventricular diastolic pressure
> 10 mmHg inspiratory drop in systolic blood pressure
Ventricular interdependence within non-distensible pericardial space
Direct needle aspiration under echocardiographic guidance
Immediate hemodynamic decompression; placement of indwelling catheter for drainage

steps.tx: The echo view surrounds the heart with a wide black **pericardial effusion** compressing the chambers. The right atrial wall buckles inward, the classic **diastolic collapse** of tamponade physiology. Pressure blocks normal filling so output falls and neck veins distend. Urgent **pericardiocentesis** with catheter drainage relieves the pressure and restores circulation.
steps.say: The ultrasound shows fluid encircling the heart with the right atrium caving in during diastole, meaning pressure outside exceeds filling pressure inside. Patients show low blood pressure, muffled heart sounds and raised neck veins, often with a marked inspiratory dip in systolic pressure. The fix is urgent echo guided drainage through a subxiphoid approach with a temporary catheter left to prevent reaccumulation and collapse.

vis.alt: The echocardiogram shows a large circumferential effusion with right atrial collapse.
